title: ChatGPT lists hereditary spastic paraplegia for Phoebe Tesoriere, 23, after four years of misdiagnosis; her GP agrees and genetic testing confirms it
summary: A Cardiff teacher put her symptoms into ChatGPT after a coma; it listed hereditary spastic paraplegia, her GP called it plausible and genetic testing confirmed it in August 2025 (BBC, WalesOnline).
account: Phoebe Tesoriere, 23, from Cardiff, Wales, a former special educational needs teacher, had a limp since childhood and from 2022 was diagnosed with epilepsy, then Todd's paralysis, and repeatedly told her symptoms were anxiety; in January 2025 she fell down stairs and spent months in hospital, and in July 2025 a seizure left her in a coma (three days per BBC Wales, 48 hours per the SWNS report in WalesOnline). After discharge she entered her symptoms into ChatGPT, which returned a list of possible conditions including hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP). She took the suggestion to her GP, who agreed it was a 'plausible reason'; genetic testing confirmed HSP, in August 2025 according to WalesOnline, which also reports the complex quadriplegic type. The first day of August is used because no day is given. There is no treatment; she uses a wheelchair, attends physiotherapy and is fundraising for a specialist chair. Cardiff and Vale University Health Board said it was 'sorry to hear about Phoebe's experience while in our care' and would not comment on an individual case. The account rests on her own statements to BBC Wales (10 April 2026) and SWNS (6 April 2026); no clinical document was fetched.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose chatbot not built or cleared for diagnosis; the patient used it to generate candidate conditions from her symptom list.
segment: Patient-initiated use of a consumer LLM
taxonomy_note: No health category exists in the taxonomy; a confirmed genetic diagnosis after four years of misdiagnosis is treated as knowledge discovery for the patient, as in the other ChatGPT diagnosis records. Only news reports exist: BBC Wales and an SWNS agency story; the health board's statement confirms she was a patient but not the diagnostic sequence.

ratings.reason: A confirmed diagnosis replaced 'anxiety' on her records and lets her plan care and equipment; the condition is progressive with no treatment, so the gain is certainty and appropriate management rather than a changed prognosis.

ai_role.statement: By her account the chatbot produced a list of candidates that included HSP; she decided to take it to her GP, the GP ordered genetic testing, and the test made the diagnosis. The prompt, the model version and the full candidate list are not reported. Only news reports quoting the patient were fetched; the health board declined to comment on the case.
